native_result.query: In which century do Diversity in Pottery Decoration and Diversity in Pottery Form show opposite growth trends for the first time, with Pottery Decoration increasing significantly and Pottery Form declining simultaneously?
native_result.HypoA: In 1700 BCE, for the first time, Diversity in Pottery Decoration shows a significant increase while Diversity in Pottery Form experiences a notable decline. This marks a unique divergence in the growth trends of these two cultural capital variables.
native_result.HypoB: Diversity in Pottery Decoration and Diversity in Pottery Form first show opposite growth trends in the 17th century BCE (the 1700 BCE bin, c. 1700-1601 BCE), i.e. during the 1800 -> 1700 BCE transition: Pottery Decoration increased significantly (Z from -0.48 to +0.97, dZ = +1.45, exceeding both the |dZ| >= 0.5 and the historical 75th-percentile |dZ| = 0.155 criteria, 94.4th percentile of all historical |dZ|) while Pottery Form declined simultaneously (Z from +0.74 to -1.13, dZ = -1.87, exceeding |dZ| >= 0.5 and P75 = 0.195, the largest decline in the whole series). No earlier bin in the 4100-500 BCE sequence shows a rising Decoration alongside a falling Form, so this is the first occurrence. We therefore hypothesize that ceramic variability was reoriented from vessel morphology to surface ornamentation in the 17th century BCE, consistent with the strongly inverse Form-Decoration relationship (r = -0.78) and rising landscape openness in the Belau pollen record (r = +0.65 with Decoration, descriptive only).
native_result.WorkflowB: 1) Loaded data/time_series_data.csv (3601 annual rows, CE -4100..-500; calBP = 1950-CE) and verified that PotteryForm/PotteryDecoration raw series have 37 100-year anchors (3564 NaNs) while the *_inter columns are NaN-free linear interpolations reproducing those anchors. 2) Cross-validated anchor values against data/capital.csv (ZKeform/Zkeverz, comma decimals, BCE = -CE): 37/37 exact matches; capital.csv and the Belau/Woserin pollen CSV treated as context/redundant. 3) Built 100-year bins sampled from the authorized *_inter series and computed bin-to-bin changes dF and dD. 4) Verified that under linear interpolation net change, OLS per-century slope and growth-rate are identical (1800->1700 BCE Decoration: +1.4500 both). 5) Derived the dual significance rule from each series' own history (36 transitions): Form median |dZ| = 0.085, P75 = 0.195; Decoration median 0.075, P75 = 0.155; criterion = |dZ| >= 0.5 AND >= P75. 6) Scanned the full chronological order -4100 -> -500 requiring dD > 0 significant AND dF < 0; exactly one bin qualifies (1700 BCE) and it is the earliest; earlier discordant candidates (4000 BCE, 1000 BCE and the 11 Form-decline bins) fail either simultaneity or magnitude. 7) Ran threshold sensitivity (|dZ| >= 0.0/0.1/0.25/0.5/1.0/1.4) and a stricter both-significant variant: the answer is invariant. 8) Reported late flat values (1700-500 BCE Form constant at -1.13) as period-aggregation artefacts, and pollen correlations as descriptive support only; exported pottery_divergence_table.csv.
